title: Two-phase KARI matching: check recipient match before parsing algorithm OID
description: try_decrypt_kari() finds a matching recipient_enc_key BEFORE calling map_kari_alg(). The comment explains: if a match is found but the algorithm is unsupported, return UnsupportedAlgorithm rather than Ok(None). This ordering is a deliberate security decision: silently returning Ok(None) when the key matches but the algorithm is unsupported would mislead the caller into thinking their key doesn't match the message. A future contributor might reorder for 'simplicity' — this would restore the misleading behavior.
close_reason: Confirmed: try_decrypt_kari (decrypt.rs lines 219-228) first scans kari.recipient_enc_keys with matches_recipient to find a matching REK, returning Ok(None) immediately if none match. Only after a recipient match is confirmed does the code check the originator type (line 234) and parse the algorithm OID via map_kari_alg (line 246). Correct two-phase design: avoids UnsupportedAlgorithm errors for KARIs that are not addressed to this key.
